Executive Summary

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION AND EMERGENCY RESPONSE POLICIES

Knead Dough Baking Company located in Bolingbrook, Illinois uses ammonia within two co-located systems for the processing and storage of bakery items. Knead Dough Baking Company's senior management is committed to offer superior service, and maintains a safety and environmental program to promote proper working conditions for all its employees and the surrounding community. Knead Dough Baking Company administers safety and environmental policies at the facility to ensure compliance with OSHAs Process Safety Management (PSM) and EPAs Risk Management Program (RMP). These programs include employee participation, training, written operating procedures, maintenance, inspections, safety committee meetings, and safety reviews/evaluations. These programs are in effect at the facility to prevent the accidental release of ammonia among other safety concerns.

STATIONARY SOURCE AND REGULATED SUBSTANCE

Knead Dough Baking Company is located at 556 St. James Gate, in Bolingbrook, Illinois. The systems were designed and constructed in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations. The facility's two systems use just over 16,000 pounds of ammonia. The majority of the system is located in the engine room including vessels and compressors. The condensers are located outside the engine room, and all of the evaporators are located in their respective cold storage rooms/areas.

ACCIDENTAL RELEASE PREVENTION PROGRAM AND CHEMICAL SPECIFIC PREVENTION STEPS

The Knead Dough Baking Company ammonia refrigeration systems have many safety features, much of which is inherent in the policies and procedures that govern the operation of the systems. For example, the facility operates in accordance with OSHA's Process Safety Management regulation and EPA's Risk Management Program (RMP).

Policies and procedures ensure safe practices are being performed. The ammonia systems
are equipped with vari

ous system controls and status indicators intended to minimize potential ammonia related accidents and to allow operators to monitor system operations. Other safety features include: ammonia sensors that sound a facility wide alarm, an emergency shutdown button that kills power to the engine room equipment, relief valves on all pressure vessels, and ventilation in the engine rooms to prevent ammonia explosions.

In addition to the Uniform Mechanical Code, the facility has based its maintenance program on the industry standard: the International Institute of Ammonia Refrigeration (IIAR) guidelines. In particular, the IIAR Bulletin 110, "Startup, Inspection, and Maintenance of Ammonia Refrigeration Systems" is used at the facility.

FIVE YEAR ACCIDENT HISTORY

An investigation into the Knead Dough Baking Company facility accident history revealed that there have been no significant releases of ammonia at the facility over the past five years that exceeded the Federal Reportable Quantity of 100 pounds. In addition, there were no injuries resulting from an ammonia release.
EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROGRAM

Knead Dough Baking Company has an Emergency Response Plan in effect at the facility. This Plan was designed to meet the following objectives:

1) Save lives;
2) Minimize and avoid injuries;
3) Protect the environment; and
4) Minimize property damage.

Knead Dough Baking Company maintains a safety committee which includes members of the designated emergency coordinators for the facility. The Plan provides the response organization and notification procedures, evacuation routes, ammonia health hazards, and mitigation procedures which will be implemented to respond effectively to emergency situations that may arise at the facility. The Plan is reviewed and updated at least once per year. This Plan is reviewed and updated to ensure compliance with the PSM and RMP regulations, as well as to incorporate any facility changes.

PLANNED CHANGES TO IMPROVE SAFETY 
The Process Hazard

Analysis (PHA) generated mitigation measures (recommendations) to improve safety at the Knead Dough Baking Company facility located at 556 St. James Gate, in Bolingbrook, Illinois. The Knead Dough Baking Company safety committee is planning to complete several items, including the recommendations, as a continual effort to provide a safe work environment for their employees. These changes include the following items:

1. Continue to train employees in the facility Safety Plan/Programs.

2. Continue to have employee involvement in Safety Plan Development.

3. Continue employee involvement through safety team participation.

4. Continue internal and external safety audits/inspections and implement changes as needed.
